subject.title: [Bug]: Teams streaming delivers normal-length replies twice in 2026.5.28

question: Should maintainers require live Microsoft Teams proof on current main before closing or changing this normal-length stream-final duplicate issue?
rationale: Source and mocked tests show the intended controller behavior, but the reported failure depends on real Teams SDK/client rendering that this read-only review cannot prove.

options.title: Run live Teams proof
options.body: Use a current-main or v2026.6.11 Teams tenant to prove normal-length and long streamed DMs before code changes or closure.

options.title: Close only with release proof
options.body: If the latest release renders one persistent bubble for the reported flow, close as implemented with the exact release and commit evidence.

options.title: Sponsor focused repair
options.body: If duplication persists, choose the stream-final collapse or fallback boundary as the repair target and require live proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Run live Teams proof
recommendation.body: Use a current-main or v2026.6.11 Teams tenant to prove normal-length and long streamed DMs before code changes or closure.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the SDK rebase and has adjacent history in the Teams reply path, making him the best routing owner for the proof or repair decision.
